You are urban_comet97, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

### Skill roots

### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)

- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)

<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

## Task context
Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll first map the documented interface and probe the reference’s main modes, then I’ll implement the highest coverage behavior in `main.py` and compare representative cases.

# Reporters

The validator writes results to stdout by default. Use `--reporter` to control the format, `--groupby` to organize results, and `--quiet` to suppress output entirely.

## Reporter types

| Reporter   | Description                    | Use case                                                |
|------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| `standard` | Human-readable table (default) | Terminal use, local development                         |
| `json`     | Structured JSON                | CI pipelines, scripting, programmatic consumption       |
| `junit`    | JUnit XML                      | Jenkins, GitLab CI, any system that reads JUnit reports |
| `sarif`    | SARIF 2.1.0                    | GitHub Code Scanning, VS Code SARIF Viewer              |

## Basic usage

```shell
validator --reporter=json .
```

## Output to a file

Append `:<path>` to the reporter name to write results to a file:

```shell
validator --reporter=json:output.json .
```

Repeat the same reporter type with different paths to write the same format to more than one file:

```shell
validator --reporter=json:summary.json --reporter=json:artifacts/summary.json .
```

Use `:-` to explicitly direct output to stdout (useful when combining reporters):

```shell
validator --reporter=json:- --reporter=junit:results.xml .
```

## Multiple reporters

Chain `--reporter` flags to produce multiple outputs in a single run:

```shell
validator --reporter=standard --reporter=json:output.json .
```

```shell
validator --reporter=junit:results.xml --reporter=sarif:results.sarif .
```

In `.cfv.toml`:

```toml
reporter = ["standard", "json:output.json"]
```

## Grouping output

:::note
Grouping only applies to the `standard` and `json` reporters.
:::

Use `--groupby` to organize the report. Supported groupings:

| Value        | Groups by                            |
|--------------|--------------------------------------|
| `filetype`   | File format (JSON, YAML, TOML, etc.) |
| `directory`  | Parent directory                     |
| `pass-fail`  | Validation result                    |
| `error-type` | Type of error (syntax, schema)       |

Combine multiple groupings:

```shell
validator --groupby=filetype,pass-fail .
```

In `.cfv.toml`:

```toml
groupby = ["filetype", "pass-fail"]
```

## Reporters

### JSON

The JSON reporter produces an array of result objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "/path/to/config.yaml",
    "status": "pass",
    "message": ""
  },
  {
    "file": "/path/to/broken.json",
    "status": "fail",
    "message": "unexpected EOF"
  }
]
```

### SARIF

The SARIF reporter produces a [SARIF 2.1.0](https://sarifweb.azurewebsites.net/) log. This integrates with:

- **GitHub Code Scanning** — upload with `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif`
- **VS Code** — view with the SARIF Viewer extension
- **Azure DevOps** — native SARIF support in pipeline results

Example GitHub Actions step:

```yaml
- name: Upload SARIF
  uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with:
    sarif_file: results.sarif
  if: always()
```

### JUnit

The JUnit reporter produces XML compatible with CI systems that consume JUnit test reports. Each validated file appears as a test case; failures include the error message.

# Filtering & Exclusion

The validator provides several ways to control which files are validated. If any filter says skip a file, it's skipped.

## Exclude directories

Use `--exclude-dirs` to skip specific subdirectories during traversal:

```shell
validator --exclude-dirs=node_modules,vendor,.git .
```

The flag accepts a comma-separated list of directory names. These are matched against directory basenames at any depth — `node_modules` excludes every `node_modules` directory in the tree, not just the top-level one.

In `.cfv.toml`:

```toml
exclude-dirs = ["node_modules", "vendor", ".git", "dist", "build"]
```

## Exclude file types

Use `--exclude-file-types` to skip files of specific types:

```shell
validator --exclude-file-types=csv,env .
```

This filters by resolved file type, not by extension. Extensionless known files (like `.gitconfig` or `.babelrc`) are excluded when they resolve to an excluded type.

JSON and JSONC are treated as a family — excluding `json` excludes both. Similarly, `yaml` covers both `.yaml` and `.yml` files.

In `.cfv.toml`:

```toml
exclude-file-types = ["csv", "env"]
```

## Include only specific file types

Use `--file-types` to validate only the listed types:

```shell
validator --file-types=json,yaml,toml .
```

`--file-types` and `--exclude-file-types` cannot be used together.

In `.cfv.toml`:

```toml
file-types = ["json", "yaml", "toml"]
```

## Recursion depth

By default, the validator recurses without limit. Use `--depth` to restrict how deep it goes:

Disable recursion (only files in the immediate search path):

```shell
validator --depth=0 .
```

Limit to 2 levels deep:

```shell
validator --depth=2 .
```

In `.cfv.toml`:

```toml
depth = 3
```

## Gitignore

Use `--gitignore` to skip files and directories matched by `.gitignore` patterns:

```shell
validator --gitignore .
```

This respects:
- `.gitignore` files at every level of the directory tree
- `.git/info/exclude`
- The global git ignore file (configured via `core.excludesFile` in `~/.gitconfig`)

The flag is only active inside a Git repository. Outside a repo, it has no effect.

In `.cfv.toml`:

```toml
gitignore = true
```

## Evaluation order

A file is validated only if it passes every active filter. During traversal, the validator checks:

1. Is the directory excluded by `--exclude-dirs`? → skip the entire directory
2. Is the file or directory matched by `.gitignore` (when `--gitignore` is active)? → skip
3. Is the file deeper than `--depth`? → skip
4. Is the file's type excluded by `--exclude-file-types`? → skip
5. Is `--file-types` set and the file's type not in the list? → skip

If none of these apply, the file is validated.

## Common configurations

### Typical project

```toml
exclude-dirs = ["node_modules", ".git", "vendor", "dist"]
gitignore = true
```

### CI pipeline (strict)

```toml
exclude-dirs = ["node_modules", "vendor"]
gitignore = true
file-types = ["json", "yaml", "toml", "xml"]
```

### Monorepo (limit scope)

```toml
exclude-dirs = ["node_modules", ".git"]
depth = 4
gitignore = true
```

# Configuration File

The validator supports a `.cfv.toml` configuration file for project-level defaults. Instead of passing flags on every invocation, define your settings once and commit them to the repository.

## Discovery

On startup, the validator looks for `.cfv.toml` in the current directory and walks up parent directories until it finds one or reaches the filesystem root.

To specify a file explicitly:

```shell
validator --config=path/to/.cfv.toml .
```

To disable auto-discovery:

```shell
validator --no-config .
```

## Precedence

Most CLI flags can also be set through [environment variables](../reference/environment-variables.md) prefixed with `CFV_`. When multiple sources set the same option, the validator resolves them in this order (highest priority first):

1. CLI flags
2. `.cfv.toml` configuration file
3. Environment variables (`CFV_*`)
4. Built-in defaults

## Example

```toml
exclude-dirs = ["node_modules", ".git", "vendor", "dist"]
exclude-file-types = ["csv"]
depth = 3
quiet = false
gitignore = true
schemastore = true
require-schema = false
reporter = ["standard"]
groupby = ["filetype", "pass-fail"]

[schema-map]
"**/package.json" = "schemas/package.schema.json"
"**/config.xml" = "schemas/config.xsd"

[type-map]
"**/inventory" = "ini"
"**/*.cfg" = "json"

[validators.csv]
delimiter = ";"
comment = "#"

[validators.json]
forbid-duplicate-keys = true
```

## All configuration keys

| Key                  | Type             | Default        | Description                                                         |
|----------------------|------------------|----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `exclude-dirs`       | array of strings | `[]`           | Subdirectories to skip during traversal                             |
| `exclude-file-types` | array of strings | `[]`           | File types to ignore                                                |
| `file-types`         | array of strings | all            | Only validate these file types                                      |
| `depth`              | integer (≥ 0)    | unlimited      | Maximum recursion depth                                             |
| `reporter`           | array of strings | `["standard"]` | Output formats: `standard`, `json`, `junit`, `sarif`                |
| `groupby`            | array of strings | `[]`           | Group output by: `filetype`, `directory`, `pass-fail`, `error-type` |
| `quiet`              | boolean          | `false`        | Suppress stdout output                                              |
| `require-schema`     | boolean          | `false`        | Fail files that support schemas but don't declare one               |
| `no-schema`          | boolean          | `false`        | Disable all schema validation                                       |
| `schemastore`        | boolean          | `false`        | Enable SchemaStore catalog lookup                                   |
| `schemastore-path`   | string           | —              | Path to local SchemaStore clone (implies `schemastore`)             |
| `globbing`           | boolean          | `false`        | Treat positional arguments as glob patterns                         |
| `gitignore`          | boolean          | `false`        | Skip files matched by `.gitignore` patterns                         |
| `schema-map`         | table            | —              | Map glob patterns to schema files                                   |
| `type-map`           | table            | —              | Map glob patterns to file types                                     |
| `validators`         | table            | —              | Per-validator options (see below)                                   |

## Schema and type maps

Both `schema-map` and `type-map` are TOML tables where keys are glob patterns and values are paths (for schemas) or type names (for type-map).

```toml
[schema-map]
"**/package.json" = "schemas/package.schema.json"
"**/pom.xml" = "schemas/maven.xsd"

[type-map]
"**/inventory" = "ini"
"**/.env.*" = "env"
```

Glob patterns follow the same syntax as `--schema-map` and `--type-map` CLI flags. See [Glob Patterns](./glob-patterns.md) for pattern syntax details.

## Validator options

Some validators accept format-specific options that control how files are parsed. These are set under `[validators.<type>]` tables.

### CSV

| Key           | Type    | Default | Description                                              |
|---------------|---------|---------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `delimiter`   | string  | `","`   | Field delimiter character. Use `"\t"` for tab-separated. |
| `comment`     | string  | —       | Lines starting with this character are skipped.          |
| `lazy-quotes` | boolean | `false` | Allow bare quotes in unquoted fields.                    |

```toml
[validators.csv]
delimiter = "\t"
comment = "#"
lazy-quotes = true
```

### JSON

| Key                     | Type    | Default | Description                                 |
|-------------------------|---------|---------|---------------------------------------------|
| `forbid-duplicate-keys` | boolean | `false` | Report duplicate keys in objects as errors. |

```toml
[validators.json]
forbid-duplicate-keys = true
```

### INI

| Key                     | Type    | Default | Description                                              |
|-------------------------|---------|---------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `forbid-duplicate-keys` | boolean | `false` | Report duplicate keys within the same section as errors. |

```toml
[validators.ini]
forbid-duplicate-keys = true
```

:::note
YAML duplicate keys are always rejected by the YAML parser regardless of configuration.
:::

## Validation of the config file itself

The `.cfv.toml` file is validated against a built-in schema on load. Typos in key names and invalid value types are reported immediately as errors (exit code 2).

```
$ validator .
Error: .cfv.toml: unknown key "exlude-dirs" (did you mean "exclude-dirs"?)
```

# Schema Validation

The validator checks syntax first. If the file parses correctly and a schema is available, it then validates the file's content against that schema.

Schemas are resolved in order:

1. **From the file** — a `$schema` property in JSON/TOML, a `yaml-language-server` comment in YAML, or an `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation` attribute in XML.
2. **From `--schema-map`** — a glob pattern mapped to a schema file.
3. **From `--schemastore`** — automatic lookup by filename against the SchemaStore catalog.

The first match wins. If no schema is found, the file passes on syntax alone.

## Declaring a schema in your files

Each format uses a different convention to reference a schema.

### JSON and JSONC

Add a `$schema` property at the top level:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/package.json",
  "name": "my-package",
  "version": "1.0.0"
}
```

### YAML

Add a `yaml-language-server` modeline comment before any content:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://json.schemastore.org/github-workflow.json
name: CI
on: push
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
```

### TOML

Add a `$schema` key at the top level:

```toml
"$schema" = "https://json.schemastore.org/pyproject.json"

[project]
name = "my-project"
version = "1.0.0"
```

### TOON

Add a quoted `"$schema"` key at the top level:

```
"$schema": https://example.com/schema.json
host: localhost
port: 5432
```

### XML

Add an `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation` attribute on the root element:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="config.xsd">
  <host>db.example.com</host>
  <port>5432</port>
</config>
```

XML uses XSD (XML Schema Definition) files rather than JSON Schema.

XML files with inline DTD declarations (`<!DOCTYPE>`) are validated against the DTD during syntax checking — no separate schema declaration needed.

### SARIF

The validator reads the `"version"` field from the file to determine whether it's SARIF 2.1.0 or 2.2, then validates against the corresponding built-in schema. No declaration needed.

## Schema references

Schema references can be:

- **URLs** — `https://json.schemastore.org/package.json`
- **Local file paths** — absolute or relative. Relative paths are resolved from the directory containing the config file being validated.

## SchemaStore integration

[SchemaStore](https://www.schemastore.org/) is a community-maintained catalog of JSON Schemas for hundreds of common config files — `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, GitHub Actions workflows, `pyproject.toml`, and many more.

With `--schemastore`, the validator matches files by name against the SchemaStore catalog and validates them against the corresponding schema. No `$schema` declaration needed in your files.

```shell
validator --schemastore .
```

Schemas are fetched on first use and cached locally. Repeated runs don't require network access.

:::info
Schemas are cached in `~/.cache/cfv/schemas/` (or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/cfv/schemas/`) with a 24-hour TTL.
:::

### Offline and restricted environments

If network access is restricted, use a local SchemaStore clone:

```shell
git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/SchemaStore/schemastore.git
```

Then point the validator at the local clone:

```shell
validator --schemastore-path=./schemastore .
```

`--schemastore-path` implies `--schemastore` — you don't need both flags.

## External schema mapping

Use `--schema-map` to apply a schema to files matching a glob pattern. This is useful when files don't declare their own schema or when you want to enforce a specific schema across a set of files.

Apply a JSON Schema to all `package.json` files:

```shell
validator --schema-map="**/package.json:schemas/package.schema.json" .
```

Apply an XSD to XML config files:

```shell
validator --schema-map="**/config.xml:schemas/config.xsd" .
```

Specify multiple mappings in one invocation:

```shell
validator \
  --schema-map="**/package.json:schemas/pkg.json" \
  --schema-map="**/*.xml:schemas/config.xsd" \
  .
```

Schema paths can be URLs, absolute paths, or relative paths. Relative paths are resolved from the current working directory.

```shell
validator --schema-map="package.json:https://json.schemastore.org/package.json" .
validator --schema-map="deploy/*.xml:/opt/schemas/config.xsd" .
validator --schema-map="src/config.yaml:schemas/app.schema.json" .
```

The same mappings can be set in `.cfv.toml`:

```toml
[schema-map]
"**/package.json" = "schemas/package.schema.json"
"**/config.xml" = "schemas/config.xsd"
```

## Priority order

When multiple schema sources are available for a file, the validator uses this precedence (highest first):

1. Schema declared in the document (`$schema`, `yaml-language-server`, `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation`)
2. `--schema-map` patterns
3. `--schemastore` catalog lookup

Document-level declarations always take priority. SchemaStore acts as a fallback for files that don't declare their own schema.

## Requiring schemas

Use `--require-schema` to fail validation on files that support schema validation but don't declare a schema:

```shell
validator --require-schema .
```

This affects JSON, JSONC, YAML, TOML, TOON, and XML files. Other formats (INI, CSV, ENV, HCL, HOCON, Properties, PList, EditorConfig, Justfile) are not affected since they have no schema mechanism.

## Disabling schema validation

Use `--no-schema` to skip all schema validation. Only syntax is checked:

```shell
validator --no-schema .
```

`--no-schema` cannot be combined with `--require-schema`, `--schema-map`, or `--schemastore`.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/reporters.py
+"""Output formatting for validation result records.
+
+Records have ``path``, ``status`` (passed/failed), and optional ``errors``.
+"""
+import html
+import json
+
+
+def _failure(r):
+    return r.get("status") in ("failed", "fail", False)
+
+
+def _record(r):
+    o = {"path": r.get("path", ""), "status": "failed" if _failure(r) else "passed"}
+    if _failure(r):
+        o["errors"] = list(r.get("errors") or [])
+    return o
+
+
+def _group(records, dimensions):
+    if not dimensions:
+        passed = sum(not _failure(r) for r in records)
+        failed = len(records) - passed
+        return {"files": [_record(r) for r in records],
+                "summary": {"passed": passed, "failed": failed}}
+    # Grouped structure follows the validator's nested files/summary shape.
+    def key(r, dim):
+        if dim == "filetype": return str(r.get("filetype", "unknown")).lower()
+        if dim == "directory":
+            import os
+            return os.path.dirname(r.get("path", "")) or "."
+        if dim == "pass-fail": return "Failed" if _failure(r) else "Passed"
+        return "syntax" if _failure(r) else "Passed"
+    def nest(items, dims, field):
+        result = {}
+        for r in items:
+            k = key(r, dims[0])
+            result.setdefault(k, []).append(r)
+        for k, vals in list(result.items()):
+            if len(dims) > 1:
+                result[k] = nest(vals, dims[1:], field)
+            elif field == "files":
+                result[k] = [_record(r) for r in vals]
+            else:
+                p = sum(not _failure(r) for r in vals)
+                result[k] = [{"passed": p, "failed": len(vals)-p}]
+        return result
+    p = sum(not _failure(r) for r in records)
+    f = len(records)-p
+    return {"files": nest(records, dimensions, "files"),
+            "summary": nest(records, dimensions, "summary"),
+            "totalPassed": p, "totalFailed": f}
+
+
+def render(records, reporter="standard", groupby=None):
+    """Return rendered output for records (without a trailing newline)."""
+    records = list(records)
+    kind = reporter.split(":", 1)[0].lower()
+    if kind == "json":
+        return json.dumps(_group(records, groupby or []), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
+    if kind == "standard":
+        lines = []
+        for r in records:
+            bad = _failure(r)
+            lines.append(f"    {'×' if bad else '✓'} {r.get('path', '')}")
+            if bad:
+                for e in r.get("errors") or []:
+                    lines.append(f"        error: {e}")
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+    if kind == "github":
+        lines = []
+        for r in records:
+            if not _failure(r): continue
+            for e in r.get("errors") or []:
+                lines.append(f"::error file={r.get('path','')}::{e}")
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+    if kind == "junit":
+        failures = sum(_failure(r) for r in records)
+        lines = ['<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>',
+                 f' <testsuites name="config-file-validator" tests="{len(records)}">',
+                 f'   <testsuite name="config-file-validator" errors="{failures}">']
+        for r in records:
+            path = html.escape(str(r.get("path", "")), quote=True)
+            lines.append(f'     <testcase name="{path} validation" classname="config-file-validator" file="{path}">')
+            if _failure(r):
+                lines.append('       <failure>')
+                for e in r.get("errors") or []:
+                    lines.append(f'         <Message>{html.escape(str(e), quote=True)}</Message>')
+                lines.extend(['       </failure>', '     </testcase>'])
+            else: lines.append('     </testcase>')
+        lines.extend(['   </testsuite>', ' </testsuites>'])
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+    return ""
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch);text(r);

"""Small syntax validators used by the CLI implementation."""
import configparser
import csv
import io
import json
import plistlib
import re
try:
    import tomllib
except ImportError:  # Python 3.10 target
    tomllib = None
    class _TomlDecodeError(ValueError): pass
    _TOML_ERROR = _TomlDecodeError
else:

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET


def _jsonc(s):
    # Remove comments while preserving quoted strings and line positions.
    out=[]; i=0; quote=False; esc=False
    while i<len(s):
        c=s[i]
        if quote:
            out.append(c)
            if esc: esc=False
            elif c=='\\': esc=True
            elif c=='"': quote=False
            i+=1; continue
        if c=='"': quote=True; out.append(c); i+=1; continue
        if s.startswith('//',i):
            start=i
            while i<len(s) and s[i]!='\n': out.append(' '); i+=1
            if i==len(s):
                line=s.count('\n',0,start)+1
                col=start-s.rfind('\n',0,start)
                raise ValueError(f'hujson: line {line}, column {col}: parsing comment: unexpected EOF')
            continue
        if s.startswith('/*',i):
            start=i
            out.extend('  '); i+=2
            while i<len(s) and not s.startswith('*/',i):
                out.append('\n' if s[i]=='\n' else ' '); i+=1
            if i<len(s): out.extend('  '); i+=2
            else:
                line=s.count('\n',0,start)+1
                col=start-s.rfind('\n',0,start)
                raise ValueError(f'hujson: line {line}, column {col}: parsing comment: unexpected EOF')
            continue
        out.append(c); i+=1
    return ''.join(out)


def _yaml(s):
    # Structural checks for common YAML errors; scalar-heavy files are accepted.
    maps = {}
    previous = None
    for n,line in enumerate(s.splitlines(),1):
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith('#') or line.strip() in ('---','...'): continue
        indent=len(line)-len(line.lstrip(' '))
        if '\t' in line[:indent]: return f"line {n}: tabs are not allowed for indentation"
        body=line.strip()
        if previous and indent > previous[0]:
            parent = previous[1]
            pm = re.match(r'^(?:-\s*)?[^:]+:\s*(.*)$', parent)
            if pm and not parent.startswith('- ') and pm.group(1) and pm.group(1) not in ('|','>','|-','>-','|+','>+'):
                return f'line {n}: mapping values are not allowed in this context'
        # Reject repeated keys in a mapping, as the reference YAML parser does.
        # Indentation gives a useful approximation of mapping scope without a
        # third-party YAML parser.
        if not body.startswith('- '):
            m = re.match(r'^(.+?):(?:\s|$)', body)
            if m:
                key = m.group(1).strip()
                for level in list(maps):
                    if level > indent: del maps[level]
                scope = maps.setdefault(indent, {})
                if key in scope:
                    return f'yaml: unmarshal errors:\n  line {n}: mapping key "{key}" already defined at line {scope[key]}'
                scope[key] = n

+            elif c in ('"',"'"): quote=c
+            elif c==',': vals.append(_scalar(body[start:i])); start=i+1
+        vals.append(_scalar(body[start:]))
+        return vals
+    try:return int(s)
+    except ValueError: return s
+
+def _fallback(text):
+    root={}; cur=root
+    for line in text.splitlines():
+        x=line.split('#',1)[0].strip()
+        if not x:continue
+        if x.startswith('[') and x.endswith(']'):
+            section=x[1:-1].strip()
+            cur=root
+            for name in section.split('.'):
+                name=name.strip().strip('"\'')
+                cur=cur.setdefault(name,{})
+            continue
+        if '=' not in x: raise ValueError('invalid TOML')
+        k,v=x.split('=',1); k=k.strip().strip('"\'')
+        cur[k]=_scalar(v)
+    return root
+
+def _load(path):
+    raw=open(path,encoding='utf-8').read()
+    return tomllib.loads(raw) if tomllib else _fallback(raw)
+
+def _env_value(key,value):
+    if key in BOOLS:
+        v=value.lower()
+        if v in ('1','t','true','true','yes'): return True
+        if v in ('0','f','false','no'): return False
+        raise ValueError(f'invalid boolean value {value!r}')
+    if key=='depth': return int(value)
+    if key in LISTS: return [x.strip() for x in value.split(',') if x.strip()]
+    return value
+
+def options(args, argv, environ=None, cwd=None):
+    """Return (namespace updates, error); CLI > config > environment > defaults."""
+    env=os.environ if environ is None else environ
+    cwd=os.getcwd() if cwd is None else cwd
+    config_path=getattr(args,'config',None)
+    no_config=getattr(args,'no_config',False)
+    data={}
+    if config_path:
+        if not os.path.isabs(config_path): config_path=os.path.join(cwd,config_path)
+        if not os.path.isfile(config_path): return {}, f'config file not found: {config_path}'
+    elif not no_config:
+        d=cwd
+        while True:
+            candidate=os.path.join(d,'.cfv.toml')
+            if os.path.isfile(candidate): config_path=candidate; break
+            parent=os.path.dirname(d)
+            if parent==d: break
+            d=parent
+    if config_path:
+        try: data=_load(config_path)
+        except Exception as e:return {}, f'{config_path}: {e}'
+    valid=set(KEYS)|{'schema-map','type-map','validators'}
+    for key in data:
+        if key not in valid:return {}, f'unknown key "{key}"'
+    cfg={k:data[k] for k in KEYS if k in data}
+    for key in ('schema-map','type-map'):
+        if key in data and isinstance(data[key],dict):
+            flag='schema_map' if key=='schema-map' else 'type_map'
+            cfg[flag]=[f'{p}:{v}' for p,v in data[key].items()]
+    updates={}
+    # Environment has lower precedence than the config file.
+    for key, attr in KEYS.items():
+        envkey='CFV_'+key.upper().replace('-','_')
+        if envkey in env:
+            try: updates[attr]=_env_value(key,env[envkey])
+            except Exception as e:return {}, f'{envkey}: {e}'
+    updates.update({KEYS.get(k,k):v for k,v in cfg.items()})
+    cli=set()
+    for token in argv:
+        if token.startswith('-'):
+            cli.add(token.lstrip('-').split('=',1)[0].replace('-','_'))
+    for k in list(updates):
+        if k.replace('_','-') in cli or k in cli: updates.pop(k,None)
+    return updates, None
*** End Patch";

def _yaml(s):
    # Structural checks for common YAML errors; scalar-heavy files are accepted.
    maps = {}
    previous = None
    open_quote = None
    quote_escape = False
    for n,line in enumerate(s.splitlines(),1):
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith('#') or line.strip() in ('---','...'): continue
        indent=len(line)-len(line.lstrip(' '))
        if '\t' in line[:indent]: return f"line {n}: tabs are not allowed for indentation"
        body=line.strip()
        continuing_quote = open_quote is not None
        if previous and indent > previous[0] and not continuing_quote:
            parent = previous[1]
            pm = re.match(r'^(?:-\s*)?[^:]+:\s*(.*)$', parent)
            if pm and not parent.startswith('- ') and pm.group(1) and pm.group(1) not in ('|','>','|-','>-','|+','>+'):
                return f'line {n}: mapping values are not allowed in this context'
        # Reject repeated keys in a mapping, as the reference YAML parser does.
        # Indentation gives a useful approximation of mapping scope without a
        # third-party YAML parser.
        if not body.startswith('- '):
            m = re.match(r'^(.+?):(?:\s|$)', body)
            if m:
                key = m.group(1).strip()
                for level in list(maps):
                    if level > indent: del maps[level]
                scope = maps.setdefault(indent, {})
                if key in scope:
                    return f'yaml: unmarshal errors:\n  line {n}: mapping key "{key}" already defined at line {scope[key]}'
                scope[key] = n
        if body.startswith((':', '- :')): return f"line {n}: could not find expected ':'"
        if body.count('[')>body.count(']') and not body.startswith('#'):
            tail=body.rsplit('[',1)[-1].strip()
            detail="did not find expected node content" if not tail else "did not find expected ',' or ']'"
            return f'line {n}: {detail}'
        if body.count('{')>body.count('}') and not body.startswith('#'):
            tail=body.rsplit('{',1)[-1].strip()
            detail="did not find expected node content" if not tail else "did not find expected ',' or '}'"
            return f'line {n}: {detail}'
        if body.count('[')<body.count(']') and not body.startswith('#'): return f"line {n}: unexpected ']'"
        if body.count('{')<body.count('}') and not body.startswith('#'): return f"line {n}: unexpected '}}'"
        i = 0
        while i < len(body):
            c = body[i]
            if open_quote:
                if open_quote == '"' and quote_escape: quote_escape = False
                elif open_quote == '"' and c == '\\': quote_escape = True
                elif open_quote == "'" and c == "'" and i + 1 < len(body) and body[i + 1] == "'": i += 1
                elif c == open_quote: open_quote = None
            elif c == '#': break
            elif c in ('"', "'") and (i == 0 or body[i - 1] in ' :[{,-'):
                open_quote = c
            i += 1
        if open_quote is None: quote_escape = False
        previous=(indent,body)
    if open_quote:
        return f'line {len(s.splitlines())+1}: found unexpected end of stream'

## Task and constraints

Reimplement `/opt/reference/executable` as a Python 3.10 program. Work in `/workspace`; only code pushed to shared `team/main` is graded. Use the executable only through its CLI. Do not run `compile.sh`; use `python3 main.py` for checks. Standard library only.

The user explicitly asked us to keep working and calling tools, review the whole program, test new cases against the reference, fix mismatches, and push. Do not stop after a status update.

## Current state

The latest shared main was fetched and merged locally at `b68d642`. Working tree is clean. `python3 -m py_compile main.py config.py validators.py reporters.py schema_validation.py gitignore.py xsd_validation.py` passed, and `python3 main.py -version` printed `validator version 2.2.2`.

Shared implementation includes CLI/path handling, config and environment options, validators, reporters, schema validation, gitignore handling, and XML/XSD support.

Notable contribution from this agent: added SARIF run checks in commit `a0b7ef2`. Generated SARIF revalidation matched the reference’s three diagnostics, in order:

- `schema: runs.0.tool.driver.language: Does not match pattern '^[a-zA-Z]{2}(-[a-zA-Z]{2})?$'`
- `schema: runs.0.language: Does not match pattern '^[a-zA-Z]{2}(-[a-zA-Z]{2})?$'`
- `schema: runs.0.newlineSequences: Array must have at least 1 items`

Also contributed reporter output fixes, schema mapping integration, and syntax diagnostic corrections. XML context marker spacing was checked against parsed reference JSON; it must contain exactly one leading space after the newline (`\n -> '' <-- around here`).

## Key constraints/preferences

- Coordinate via `mcp__swarm__post` and read teammate work with `mcp__swarm__read_feed`.
- Before pushing, fetch `team`, merge `team/main`, then push `HEAD:main`; teammates push concurrently.
- Keep the implementation independent; never invoke the reference at runtime.
- The user expects active work to continue, not an early wrap-up.

## Next steps

1. Continue whole-program reference comparisons on fresh option combinations and error paths.
2. Check group feed for remaining claimed/failing areas before editing to avoid duplication. Latest feed indicates XML XSD target namespace handling was just added; SARIF checks are confirmed present.
3. For any mismatch, reproduce against both reference and `python3 main.py`, patch, compile-check, commit, fetch/merge, and push.
4. Re-fetch team main before concluding; shared code may have changed since this checkpoint.
I’ll review the current shared implementation and the latest group notes, then probe an uncovered behavior against the reference and push any concrete fix.

Config File Validator

Config File Validator validates config files across 17 formats. It recursively searches directories for config files, detects their format by extension or filename, and reports errors. ## Install **Homebrew** ```shell brew install config-file-validator ``` **Winget** ```shell winget install Boeing.config-file-validator ``` **Go Install** ```shell go install github.com/Boeing/config-file-validator/v2/cmd/validator@latest ```
More install options **MacPorts** ```shell sudo port install config-file-validator ``` **Scoop** ```shell scoop install config-file-validator ``` **Binary releases** Download pre-built binaries for macOS, Linux, and Windows from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Boeing/config-file-validator/releases).
## Usage Validate all config files in the current directory: See the [CLI reference](https://boeing.github.io/config-file-validator/docs/reference/cli-flags) for all options. ## Features - Schema validation via JSON Schema, XSD, and automatic [SchemaStore](https://www.schemastore.org/) lookup - Auto-detects file types by extension and [known filename](https://boeing.github.io/config-file-validator/docs/reference/known-files) - JSON, JUnit, and SARIF output for CI pipelines - [GitHub Action](https://github.com/Boeing/validate-configs-action) with PR annotations - [Pre-commit hook](https://boeing.github.io/config-file-validator/docs/integrations/pre-commit) - Project-level [`.cfv.toml`](https://boeing.github.io/config-file-validator/docs/guides/configuration-file) configuration - Usable as a [Go library](https://boeing.github.io/config-file-validator/docs/integrations/go-library) ## Documentation Documentation is hosted at https://boeing.github.io/config-file-validator. ## Contributing We welcome contributions! See the [contributing guide](./CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Contributors ## License [Apache 2.0](./LICENSE)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, os, json, glob, argparse, time

from pathlib import Path

from gitignore import repository_root, ignored

from xsd_validation import validate_xml_xsd
from config import _parse as parse_toml
from config import load_options, load_environment

VERSION = "2.2.2"
HELP = '''Usage: validator [OPTIONS] [<search_path>...]

positional arguments:

Schema validation runs automatically when a file declares a schema:
  JSON:  {"$schema": "schema.json", ...}

    \tA comma separated list of file types to ignore
  -file-types string

  -gitignore
    \tSkip files and directories matched by .gitignore patterns.
  -globbing
    \tIf globbing flag is set, check for glob patterns in the arguments.
  -groupby string
    \tGroup output by filetype, directory, pass-fail, error-type. Supported for Standard and JSON reports
  -no-config
    \tDisable automatic discovery of .cfv.toml configuration files.

  -quiet

  -require-schema
    \tFail validation if a file supports schema validation but does not declare a schema.
    \tSupported types: JSON ($schema property), YAML (yaml-language-server comment),
    \tTOML ($schema key), TOON ("$schema" key), XML (xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation).
    \tOther file types (INI, CSV, ENV, HCL, HOCON, Properties, PList, EditorConfig) are not affected.
    \tCannot be used with --no-schema.
  -schema-map value
    \tMap a glob pattern to a schema file for validation.
    \tFormat: <pattern>:<schema_path>
    \tUse JSON Schema (.json) for JSON, YAML, TOML, and TOON files.
    \tUse XSD (.xsd) for XML files. Paths are relative to the current directory.
    \tMultiple mappings can be specified.
    \tExamples:
    \t  --schema-map="**/package.json:schemas/package.schema.json"
    \t  --schema-map="**/config.xml:schemas/config.xsd"
  -schemastore

EXTS = {'.json':'json','.jsonc':'jsonc','.yaml':'yaml','.yml':'yaml','.toml':'toml','.xml':'xml','.toon':'toon','.sarif':'sarif','.hcl':'hcl','.tf':'hcl','.ini':'ini','.env':'env','.csv':'csv','.properties':'properties','.editorconfig':'editorconfig','.plist':'plist'}
KNOWN = {'.babelrc':'jsonc','.eslintrc':'jsonc','.eslintrc.json':'jsonc','tsconfig.json':'jsonc','jsconfig.json':'jsonc','.swcrc':'jsonc','.jshintrc':'jsonc','.arcconfig':'json','.watchmanconfig':'json','composer.lock':'json','bun.lock':'json','deno.lock':'json','flake.lock':'json','pipfile':'toml','cargo.lock':'toml','poetry.lock':'toml','uv.lock':'toml','pdm.lock':'toml','.gitconfig':'ini','.gitmodules':'ini','.npmrc':'ini','.pylintrc':'ini','.flake8':'ini','.curlrc':'ini','.nanorc':'ini','.clang-format':'yaml','.clang-tidy':'yaml','.clangd':'yaml','.gemrc':'yaml','.env':'env','.editorconfig':'editorconfig','pom.xml':'xml','build.xml':'xml','ant.xml':'xml','.classpath':'xml','.project':'xml','justfile':'justfile','.justfile':'justfile'}
ALIASES={'jsonc':'json','yml':'yaml','just':'justfile'}

def declares_schema(typ, content):
    t=ALIASES.get(typ,typ)
    if t in ('json','jsonc','sarif'):
        try:
            doc=json.loads(content) if t!='jsonc' else json.loads(re.sub(r',\s*([}\]])',r'\1',_jsonc(content)))
            return isinstance(doc,dict) and '$schema' in doc
        except Exception: return False
    if t=='yaml': return bool(re.search(r'yaml-language-server:\s*\$schema\s*=\s*\S+',content))
    if t=='toml': return bool(re.search(r'^\s*["\']?\$schema["\']?\s*=',content,re.M))
    if t=='toon': return bool(re.search(r'^\s*["\']\$schema["\']\s*:',content,re.M))
    if t=='xml': return 'noNamespaceSchemaLocation' in content
    return True

def schema_error_location(content, message):
    """Approximate the source location of a JSON Schema property error."""
    match=re.match(r'([^:]+):',message)
    if not match or match.group(1)=='(root)': return 1,1
    key=match.group(1).split('.')[-1].strip('[]')
    if not key: return 1,1
    found=re.search(r'"'+re.escape(key)+r'"\s*:',content)
    if not found: return 1,1
    before=content[:found.start()]
    return before.count('\n')+1, len(before.rsplit('\n',1)[-1])+1

def schemastore_catalog(root):
    if not root:
        return None
    path=os.path.join(root,'src','api','json','catalog.json')
    try:
        with open(path,encoding='utf-8') as f:
            value=json.load(f)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        runtime_error(f'opening schemastore: reading schemastore catalog: open {path}: no such file or directory')
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        runtime_error(f'opening schemastore: reading schemastore catalog: {e}')
        return False
    if not isinstance(value,dict) or not isinstance(value.get('schemas'),list):
        runtime_error('opening schemastore: reading schemastore catalog: invalid catalog format')
        return False
    return value['schemas']

def find_schemastore_schema(catalog, root, filepath):
    if not catalog:
        return None
    basename=os.path.basename(filepath)
    rel=os.path.relpath(filepath,os.getcwd()).replace(os.sep,'/')
    for entry in catalog:
        if not isinstance(entry,dict):
            continue
        matches=entry.get('fileMatch',[])
        if isinstance(matches,str):
            matches=[matches]
        if not isinstance(matches,list):
            continue
        if not any(isinstance(p,str) and (glob.fnmatch.fnmatch(basename,p) or glob.fnmatch.fnmatch(rel,p) or glob.fnmatch.fnmatch(filepath,p)) for p in matches):
            continue
        url=entry.get('url')
        if not isinstance(url,str) or not url:
            continue
        if os.path.isabs(url) and os.path.isfile(url):
            return url
        if not url.startswith(('http://','https://')):
            candidate=os.path.abspath(os.path.join(root,url))
            if os.path.isfile(candidate):
                return candidate
        else:
            name=os.path.basename(url.split('?',1)[0])
            candidate=os.path.join(root,'src','schemas','json',name)
            if os.path.isfile(candidate):
                return candidate
        return url
    return None

def parser():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    p.add_argument('paths',nargs='*'); p.add_argument('-h','--help',action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('-version','--version',action='store_true'); p.add_argument('-depth',type=int,default=-1)
    p.add_argument('-exclude-dirs',default=''); p.add_argument('-exclude-file-types',default=''); p.add_argument('-file-types',default='')
    p.add_argument('-globbing',action='store_true'); p.add_argument('-quiet',action='store_true'); p.add_argument('-gitignore',action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('-no-schema',action='store_true'); p.add_argument('-require-schema',action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('-reporter',action='append',default=[]); p.add_argument('-groupby',default='')
    p.add_argument('-no-config',action='store_true'); p.add_argument('-config'); p.add_argument('-schema-map',action='append',default=[]); p.add_argument('-schemastore',action='store_true'); p.add_argument('-schemastore-path'); p.add_argument('-type-map',action='append',default=[])
    return p

def detect(path, maps):
    name=os.path.basename(path).lower()
    rel=os.path.relpath(path, os.getcwd()).replace(os.sep, '/')
    for pair in maps:
        pat,sep,typ=pair.partition(':')
        if sep and (glob.fnmatch.fnmatch(path,pat) or glob.fnmatch.fnmatch(rel,pat) or glob.fnmatch.fnmatch('./'+rel,pat)):
            return typ.lower()
    if name in KNOWN:return KNOWN[name]
    return EXTS.get(Path(path).suffix.lower())

def usage_error(message):
    marker='optional flags:'
    head, _, tail=HELP.partition(marker)
    print(message)
    print(head.rstrip()+'\n\n'+marker)
    print(tail.strip('\n'),file=sys.stderr)

def runtime_error(message, cli=False):
    prefix=datetime.now().astimezone().strftime('%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S')+' An error occurred'
    if cli: prefix+=' during CLI execution'
    print(prefix+': '+message,file=sys.stderr)

def main():
    p=parser()
    # The reference accepts both Go-style single dash and conventional long flags.
    argv=[('-'+x[2:]) if x.startswith('--') else x for x in sys.argv[1:]]
    takes_value={'-depth','-exclude-dirs','-exclude-file-types','-file-types','-groupby','-reporter','-config','-schema-map','-type-map','-schemastore-path'}
    option_end=len(argv); scan=0
    while scan<len(argv):
        token=argv[scan]
        if token=='--' or token=='-' or not token.startswith('-'):
            option_end=scan; break
        option=token.split('=',1)[0]

    bool_flags={'-version','-quiet','-globbing','-gitignore','-no-schema','-require-schema','-schemastore','-no-config','-help','-h'}
    takes_value={'-depth','-exclude-dirs','-exclude-file-types','-file-types','-groupby','-reporter','-config','-schema-map','-type-map','-schemastore-path'}
    explicit_bool_flags=set()
    raw_i=0
    while raw_i < len(argv):
        token=argv[raw_i]
        if token == '--' or not token.startswith('-') or token == '-':

        if key in bool_flags:

        raw_i += 2 if key in takes_value and '=' not in token else 1
    normalized=[]
    for index, token in enumerate(argv):
        if index>=option_end:

        key, eq, value=token.partition('=')

            elif value.lower() not in ('false','0'):

        option=token.split('=',1)[0]
        i += 2 if option in takes_value and '=' not in token else 1
    depth_explicit = any(t == '-depth' or t.startswith('-depth=') for t in (argv[:split] if split is not None else argv))

    explicit_flags = {t.split('=', 1)[0].lstrip('-') for t in cli_tokens if t.startswith('-') and t != '-'} | explicit_bool_flags
    if split is not None:

    a=p.parse_args(argv)
    _, env_error = load_environment()
    if env_error:
        usage_error('parse error')
        return 2
    if depth_explicit and a.depth < 0:
        usage_error('wrong parameter value for depth, value cannot be negative')
        return 2
    if a.help:
        marker = 'optional flags:'
        head, _, tail = HELP.partition(marker)
        print(head.rstrip() + '\n\n' + marker)
        print(tail.strip('\n'), file=sys.stderr)
        return 0
    if a.version: print('validator version '+VERSION);return 0
    config_options, config_error = load_options(a.config, a.no_config)
    if config_error:
        print(datetime.now().astimezone().strftime('%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S') + ' An error occurred: ' + config_error, file=sys.stderr)

    option_dest = {
        'depth': 'depth', 'exclude-dirs': 'exclude_dirs',
        'exclude-file-types': 'exclude_file_types', 'file-types': 'file_types',
        'reporter': 'reporter', 'groupby': 'groupby', 'quiet': 'quiet',

        'globbing': 'globbing', 'gitignore': 'gitignore',

            elif key == 'groupby' and isinstance(value, list):
                value = ','.join(value)
            elif key == 'reporter' and isinstance(value, str):
                value = [value]
            setattr(a, dest, value)

# CLI Flags

```
validator [OPTIONS] [<search_path>...]
```

If no search path is provided, the validator searches the current directory. Use `-` to read from stdin (requires `--file-types`).

## Flags

| Flag                  | Type   | Default    | Description                                                                                                        |
|-----------------------|--------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `-depth`              | int    | unlimited  | Maximum recursion depth. `0` disables recursion.                                                                   |
| `-exclude-dirs`       | string | —          | Comma-separated list of directory names to skip.                                                                   |
| `-exclude-file-types` | string | —          | Comma-separated list of file types to ignore. Cannot be used with `-file-types`.                                   |
| `-file-types`         | string | all        | Comma-separated list of file types to validate. Cannot be used with `-exclude-file-types`.                         |
| `-gitignore`          | bool   | `false`    | Skip files matched by `.gitignore` patterns. Only active inside a Git repository.                                  |
| `-globbing`           | bool   | `false`    | Treat positional arguments as glob patterns.                                                                       |
| `-groupby`            | string | —          | Group output by: `filetype`, `directory`, `pass-fail`, `error-type`. Comma-separated.                              |
| `-quiet`              | bool   | `false`    | Suppress all stdout output. Errors still print to stderr.                                                          |
| `-reporter`           | string | `standard` | Output format and optional path. Format: `<type>:<path>`. Types: `standard`, `json`, `junit`, `sarif`. Repeatable. |
| `-require-schema`     | bool   | `false`    | Fail files that support schema validation but don't declare a schema.                                              |
| `-no-schema`          | bool   | `false`    | Disable all schema validation. Cannot be combined with `-require-schema`, `-schema-map`, or `-schemastore`.        |
| `-schema-map`         | string | —          | Map a glob pattern to a schema file. Format: `<pattern>:<schema_path>`. Repeatable.                                |
| `-schemastore`        | bool   | `false`    | Enable automatic schema lookup by filename using the SchemaStore catalog.                                          |
| `-schemastore-path`   | string | —          | Path to a local SchemaStore clone. Implies `-schemastore`.                                                         |
| `-config`             | string | auto       | Path to a `.cfv.toml` configuration file.                                                                          |
| `-no-config`          | bool   | `false`    | Disable automatic `.cfv.toml` discovery.                                                                           |
| `-type-map`           | string | —          | Map a glob pattern to a file type. Format: `<pattern>:<type>`. Repeatable.                                         |
| `-version`            | bool   | —          | Print the version and exit.                                                                                        |

---

# Supported File Types

| Format          | Extensions              | Syntax | Schema |
|-----------------|-------------------------|:------:|:------:|
| JSON            | `.json`                 |   ✅    |   ✅    |
| JSONC           | `.jsonc`                |   ✅    |   ✅    |
| YAML            | `.yaml`, `.yml`         |   ✅    |   ✅    |
| TOML            | `.toml`                 |   ✅    |   ✅    |
| XML             | `.xml`                  |   ✅    |   ✅    |
| TOON            | `.toon`                 |   ✅    |   ✅    |
| SARIF           | `.sarif`                |   ✅    |   ✅    |
| HCL             | `.hcl`, `.tf`           |   ✅    |   —    |
| INI             | `.ini`, `.cfg`          |   ✅    |   —    |
| HOCON           | `.conf`                 |   ✅    |   —    |
| ENV             | `.env`                  |   ✅    |   —    |
| CSV             | `.csv`                  |   ✅    |   —    |
| Properties      | `.properties`           |   ✅    |   —    |
| EDITORCONFIG    | `.editorconfig`         |   ✅    |   —    |
| Justfile        | `justfile`, `.justfile` |   ✅    |   —    |
| Apple PList XML | `.plist`                |   ✅    |   —    |

## Schema types

- JSON, JSONC, YAML, TOML, and TOON files are validated against [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/).
- XML files are validated against [XSD](https://www.w3.org/XML/Schema) (XML Schema Definition).
- SARIF files are validated against a built-in schema matched to the file's version field.

## File type families

- `json` includes both JSON and JSONC for filtering purposes (`--file-types`, `--exclude-file-types`).
- `yaml` includes both `.yaml` and `.yml`.

## Known files

Many files are recognized by filename regardless of extension. See [Known Files](./known-files.md).
